constant.proof_md:
# Proof and scope

For Q symmetric positive definite with spectrum in [mu, L], 0 < eta < 2 / L and q = max(|1-eta*mu|, |1-eta*L|) < 1, the iterates x[k+1] = (I-eta*Q)x[k] - eta*e[k], with ||e[k]|| <= epsilon[k], satisfy

||x[k]|| <= q^k ||x[0]|| + eta sum(s=0..k-1) q^(k-1-s) epsilon[s].

Diagonalize Q in an orthonormal eigenbasis. The spectral norm of I-eta*Q is at most q. Applying the triangle inequality gives ||x[k+1]|| <= q||x[k]|| + eta*epsilon[k]. Induction unrolls this recurrence into the stated bound.

For a uniformly bounded error, the geometric series is at most 1/(1-q). If eta <= 1/L, the endpoint factors are nonnegative and q=1-eta*mu.

## Corollary
If epsilon[s] <= epsilon, limsup ||x[k]|| <= eta*epsilon/(1-q). For eta <= 1/L, q=1-eta*mu and the bound becomes epsilon/mu.

## Skeptic counterexample
In one dimension, take Q=mu, x[0]=0 and e[k]=epsilon. Then x[k] = -(epsilon/mu)(1-(1-eta*mu)^k), so x[k] tends to -epsilon/mu instead of zero.

This is a standard illustrative task, not a claim of novelty or formal verification.

# Inexact Gradient Descent: A Residual Bound - Revised v2

Authored reference manuscript. No model calls; no novelty or conference acceptance claim.

## Abstract
For step sizes up to 1/L, bounded gradient error gives an asymptotic residual bound of epsilon / mu. Constant bias can attain this bound.

## Setting and theorem
For Q symmetric positive definite with spectrum in [mu, L], 0 < eta < 2 / L and q = max(|1-eta*mu|, |1-eta*L|) < 1, the iterates x[k+1] = (I-eta*Q)x[k] - eta*e[k], with ||e[k]|| <= epsilon[k], satisfy

||x[k]|| <= q^k ||x[0]|| + eta sum(s=0..k-1) q^(k-1-s) epsilon[s].

If epsilon[s] <= epsilon, limsup ||x[k]|| <= eta*epsilon/(1-q). For eta <= 1/L, q=1-eta*mu and the bound becomes epsilon/mu.

## Proof
Diagonalize Q in an orthonormal eigenbasis. The spectral norm of I-eta*Q is at most q. Applying the triangle inequality gives ||x[k+1]|| <= q||x[k]|| + eta*epsilon[k]. Induction unrolls this recurrence into the stated bound.

For a uniformly bounded error, the geometric series is at most 1/(1-q). If eta <= 1/L, the endpoint factors are nonnegative and q=1-eta*mu.

## Boundary case
In one dimension, take Q=mu, x[0]=0 and e[k]=epsilon. Then x[k] = -(epsilon/mu)(1-(1-eta*mu)^k), so x[k] tends to -epsilon/mu instead of zero.

## Numerical check
Q=diag(1,10), eta=0.1, x[0]=(1,1), e[k]=(0.10,0). 81 saved states; the proved bound holds at all of them. Final norm at k=80: 0.09975968. Numerical agreement is not a proof.

## Review and revision
R1: Make the spectral assumptions and step-size range explicit in the theorem. R2: Complete the geometric-series bound and its constant-bias boundary case.

Added the spectral assumptions and complete supporting argument. The established research conclusion is retained; numerical evidence remains separate from the proof.

## Limitations
Known quadratic result; no claim for general nonlinear objectives. Model reviews in the full EAR engine are not formal proof or conference acceptance. The review above is prepared demonstration feedback.

## Reference
Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, chapter 9.
https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/
